This distinction challenges indiscriminate glycolytic inhibition and favors interventions matched to the affected clearance step. Defective efferocytosis may amplify synovitis through persistence of cellular debris and loss of resolution-promoting signals, thereby creating an environment unfavorable to cartilage homeostasis. Emerging receptor-directed, metabolic, and intra-articular delivery strategies offer opportunities to restore clearance, but clinical validation remains necessary. Translation will require identification of susceptible macrophage populations, functional assessment of the complete efferocytic process, and demonstration that clearance recovery mediates meaningful improvements in joint structure and symptoms.

articles.titulo: Lactate dynamics at the Pseudomonas aeruginosa-host interface: bacterial metabolism, host defense, and emerging links to histone lactylation.
articles.autores: Jian Y, Wu Z, Liang Y, Cao J, Li M, Yang F, Wang K
articles.resumo_original: At the Pseudomonas aeruginosa-host interface, lactate is both a host immunometabolic product and a preferred bacterial carbon source. Its local concentration reflects host production, bacterial utilization, transport, and clearance rather than inflammation alone. P. aeruginosa uses D- and L-lactate through stereospecific, conditionally regulated systems. It preferentially consumes lactate in human burn-wound exudate, and this capacity contributes to early intracellular survival in macrophages. Lactate-associated acidity also increases bacterial vesicle release and quinolone signaling, weakening antimicrobial-peptide activity independently of chromatin modification. On the host side, bacterial L-lactate utilization and virulence-factor-associated suppression of epithelial glycolysis lower epithelial lactate and histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la). These changes are linked to disrupted RNA regulation and impaired ciliary clearance. In macrophages, the quorum-sensing signal 2-aminoacetophenone (2-AA) reprograms bioenergetics, autophagy, and lipid metabolism, promoting tolerance and intracellular persistence. A separate hypothesis connecting 2-AA to increased macrophage lactate and H3K18la is supported only by a supplement abstract and requires full-length validation. Histone lactylation is therefore an emerging extension of this biology. This narrative review follows two linked strands: bacterial lactate utilization and lactate-associated changes in host defense. It distinguishes established metabolic effects from proposed lactylation-dependent mechanisms and considers potential therapeutic directions and their trade-offs. These include targeting bacterial lactate utilization, airway acidity, host transport or modification enzymes, and 2-AA-associated tolerance. Any benefit must be assessed against the possibility of supplying bacterial nutrients or worsening host injury.

articles.titulo: Cachexia and Sarcopenia in Patients with Coexisting Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
articles.autores: Oskin D, Kotlyarov S
articles.resumo_original: Malnutrition, loss of muscle mass, and reduced muscle strength are common but underrecognized conditions in tuberculosis (TB) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). These abnormalities may persist after completion of TB treatment, and a normal or elevated body mass index does not exclude muscle depletion. Unlike the extensively studied conditions of hyperglycemia and obesity, the catabolic end of the spectrum of metabolic disturbances in coexisting TB and COPD remains insufficiently investigated. This narrative review focuses on cachexia and sarcopenia in patients with coexisting TB and COPD (TB-COPD). It examines the roles of systemic inflammation, immunometabolic remodeling, mitochondrial dysfunction, disturbances in protein metabolism and endocrine regulation, and ceramide signaling. Because direct evidence in TB-COPD is scarce, findings from TB or post-tuberculosis lung disease without confirmed COPD and from COPD alone are used as indirect evidence, and the level of evidence is indicated for each mechanism. The diagnostic approach is organized around current clinical guidelines and includes assessment of nutritional status, diagnosis of malnutrition using the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria, identification of sarcopenia using European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 (EWGSOP2) or Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) criteria, pulmonary function testing to distinguish post-tuberculosis airflow obstruction from COPD, and evaluation for reversible causes of muscle weakness. The main treatment approaches are correction of malnutrition, pulmonary rehabilitation, and treatment of the underlying respiratory disease. The effectiveness of interventions is assessed through changes in muscle strength, physical performance, body weight, and body composition. The evidence base for patients with coexisting TB and COPD remains limited; most studies have investigated each disease separately. The efficacy of pharmacological agents targeting the molecular mechanisms of muscle wasting has not been established in this population. Priorities for future research include prospective assessment of muscle function in TB-COPD cohorts and the development of personalized strategies for nutritional and rehabilitation support.

articles.titulo: Beyond Histocompatibility: Donor Tissue Immune States and Their Role in Heart Transplantation.
articles.autores: Urbanowicz T, Kowalewski M, Suwalski P, Raffa GM
articles.resumo_original: Heart transplantation transfers not only donor alloantigens and functional myocardium but also a pre-existing tissue environment shaped by resident immune, vascular, stromal, and parenchymal populations. This review examines the hypothesis that the biological state of donor tissue influences subsequent recipient immunity and contributes to heterogeneity in allograft outcomes. Donor-resident macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, and tissue-resident lymphocytes constitute an immunologically active myocardial niche that encounters ischemia-reperfusion injury and recipient immune effectors immediately after implantation. Experimental and human studies demonstrate the dynamic coexistence and replacement of donor- and recipient-derived immune populations, with recipient cells acquiring phenotypes within the graft microenvironment. We distinguish transient donor-tissue activation from genuine tissue immune memory, which would require persistence of an exposure-induced molecular or functional state and an altered response to a subsequent challenge. Potential mechanisms include trained innate immunity, epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, endothelial inflammatory memory, and persistent stromal-immune interactions. We propose that allograft biology be investigated at the level of the donor-recipient immune pair and outline longitudinal single-cell, spatial, and cell-of-origin approaches to test this concept in human heart transplantation.

articles.titulo: Lipidomic Remodelling and Low Sperm Quality Associated with High-Fat Diet-Induced Gut Microbial Dysbiosis in Mice.
articles.autores: Pan M, Scarlata E, Hui F, Xia J, O'Flaherty C
articles.resumo_original: Infertility affects one in six couples worldwide, with male infertility contributing to ~50% of cases. Rising obesity rates have been linked to impaired male fertility, potentially through alterations in the gut microbiota; however, underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We characterized gut microbiome composition and lipidomic profiles in stool, serum, and testis samples. We assessed sperm quality in C57BL6 male mice fed a 45% fat diet (high-fat diet, HFD) or a 10% fat diet (normal diet, ND). We analyzed the gut microbiota by 16S rRNA sequencing. We measured short-chain fatty acids by gas chromatography. We performed untargeted lipidomic profiling of stool, serum, and testis using UPLC-MS/MS. CASA and cytochemical and immunocytochemical analyses assessed sperm quality and oxidative stress markers. HFD-fed mice exhibited gut microbiota dysbiosis characterized by an increased Bacillota/Bacteroidota ratio, altered bacterial community composition, increased acetic acid, and reduced butyric acid. Lipidomic analyses revealed distinct stool, serum, and testis lipid profiles, including increased abundance of gut microbiota-associated lipids containing odd-chain fatty acyl groups in HFD-fed mice. These alterations were accompanied by reduced sperm motility, impaired acrosomal integrity, epididymal sperm maturation and sperm capacitation, and elevated oxidative and nitrosative stress. Collectively, these findings support a gut-testis-epididymis axis in which altered gut microbiota-derived lipids contribute to oxidative stress and reduced sperm quality.

articles.titulo: Prophylactic Soraphen A Treatment Attenuates Western Diet-Exacerbated IMQ-Induced Psoriasiform Inflammation.
articles.autores: Kao YS, Kommoss KS, Bieler T, Godoy GJ, Lopez Krol A, Boukhallouk F, Kommoss FKF, Heide D, Kirsch SH, Müller R, Heikenwälder M, Sparwasser T
articles.resumo_original: Psoriasis is a T-cell-mediated inflammatory disease amplified by metabolic stress. Acetyl-CoA carboxylase 1 (ACC1)-dependent fatty acid synthesis is required for IL-17-producing T cells. Here, we asked whether short-term systemic administration of soraphen A (SorA), a dual ACC1/2 inhibitor, modulates imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasiform inflammation under normal diet (ND) and Western diet (WD) conditions. Female C57BL/6J mice were fed ND or WD for 12 weeks prior to daily intraperitoneal injections of SorA or vehicle for 10 days, followed by 5 days of topical IMQ to induce psoriasiform dermatitis. Disease severity was assessed by macroscopic, histological, transcriptional, and flow cytometric readouts. Prophylactic SorA administration had no measurable effect in ND-fed mice. In WD-fed mice, prophylactic SorA reduced erythema, back skin thickening, and epidermal hyperplasia, whereas scaling remained unchanged. Selected histological skin readouts were numerically lower, whereas the qPCR panel showed no statistically significant differences. In skin-draining lymph nodes, IL-17A+ CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell frequencies and numbers were significantly reduced, whereas γδT17 cells did not differ significantly. Hepatic steatosis scores were unchanged, but hepatic neutrophil infiltration was reduced. Under the present prophylactic regimen, systemic SorA administration was associated with modest attenuation of WD-exacerbated IMQ-induced psoriasiform inflammation. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of ACC-targeted immunometabolic interventions in metabolically aggravated psoriasiform inflammation.

articles.titulo: Integrating Host Transcriptomics and Metagenomics in the Periparturient Dairy Cow: From Molecular Signatures to Host-Microbiome Interfaces.
articles.autores: Ma Q, Tharwat M, Ullah A, Liu J, Alkheraif AA, Khan MZ
articles.resumo_original: The periparturient or transition period-roughly three weeks before to three weeks after calving-compresses the most severe metabolic, endocrine and immunological demands of the production cycle into a few weeks and accounts for most clinical disease and involuntary culling in dairy herds. Conventional surveillance relies on downstream indicators-non-esterified fatty acids, β-hydroxybutyrate, calcium and acute-phase proteins-that document failed adaptation without resolving its regulatory origins. Two omics platforms now close that gap. Transcriptomics shows that the liver, adipose tissue, mammary gland, endometrium, rumen epithelium and circulating leukocytes each execute a distinct, temporally ordered program organized around lipid mobilization, gluconeogenesis, endoplasmic reticulum stress, redox defense and inflammatory resolution, layered over a regulatory tier of non-coding RNAs. Metagenomics shows in parallel that rumen, hindgut, uterine, vaginal, teat-apex and colostrum communities are restructured by parturition and by the dietary shift into lactation, with reproducible dysbiotic signatures accompanying ketosis, fatty liver, metritis, endometritis and intramammary infection. Critically, the two layers are mechanistically coupled: microbial short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, purine derivatives and amino acids reprogram hepatic and immune cell transcription, while host lipolysis, inflammation and mineral demand reshape community structure. This review synthesizes both groups of literature within a single framework, formalizes five host-microbiome interfaces supported by paired measurements and identifies the biomarker, nutritional and genetic-selection opportunities that emerge only when host and microbial evidence are read together.

articles.titulo: NLRC3 deficiency exacerbates high-fat diet-induced enteric nervous system injury and colonic motility dysfunction in mice via activating NF-κB signaling pathway.
articles.revista: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
articles.autores: Wang Y, Li Y, Li MY, Tao SS, Tan GH, Li YQ
articles.resumo_original: A high-fat diet (HFD) induces low-grade intestinal inflammation, thereby causing structural and functional impairments of the enteric nervous system (ENS). Nucleotide oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptor (NLR) containing a caspase activation and recruitment domain 3 (NLRC3) participates in key pathophysiological processes related to inflammation, immunity, and proliferative diseases. However, the function of NLRC3 within the ENS remains to be clarified. This investigation was designed to characterize NLRC3 expression and distribution within the ENS and to elucidate its mechanism in modulating ENS injury. An HFD-induced low-grade colonic inflammation model was established in NLRC3 gene knockout (Nlrc3-/-) mice and wild-type (WT) C57BL/6J mice. The influence of NLRC3 on ENS architecture and motor function was assessed using morphological evaluation, molecular biological assays, and colonic motility analyses. The findings demonstrated that NLRC3 was primarily distributed within the cytoplasm of ENS neurons in mice, with HFD decreasing NLRC3 expression in enteric neurons. Relative to WT mice, HFD-treated Nlrc3-/- mice developed more pronounced ENS injury, characterized by enteric glial cells proliferation and activation, enteric neuronal loss accompanied by structural disruption, and a further delay in colonic transit function. NLRC3 deficiency exacerbated HFD-induced ENS injury and enteric neuronal apoptosis via nuclear factor-κB signaling pathway activation. These observations establish NLRC3 as a key negative regulator of neuroinflammatory responses in the ENS. As a negative regulatory pattern recognition receptor that links innate immunity with ENS signaling, NLRC3 may represent a promising therapeutic target.

articles.titulo: A modular in vitro multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of high-value vidarabine 5'-monophosphate from adenosine.
articles.autores: Su W, Zhang X, Li R, Li K, Guo X, Liu X, Wang Z, Wang H, Liu Y
articles.resumo_original: Nucleoside analogues such as vidarabine (Ara-A) are vital therapeutics but are often limited by poor pharmacokinetics. Its phosphorylated form, vidarabine 5'-monophosphate (Ara-AMP), offers improved solubility and is used as a clinical alternative, although it can be dephosphorylated to Ara-A in vivo. Here, we report a modular multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of Ara-AMP directly from adenosine. The cascade integrates three functional modules: a core module (PNP, PPM, and RpiA) for the conversion of adenosine to Ara-A, a driver module (dNKδ20) for the selective phosphorylation of Ara-A to Ara-AMP, and a support module (PPK) for ATP regeneration from low-cost ADP and polyphosphate. The use of dNKδ20, a mutant deoxyribonucleoside kinase with high selectivity for Ara-A over adenosine, is critical for minimizing the formation of AMP byproduct, which would otherwise complicate downstream processing. Under optimized conditions, the cascade achieved an 80.2% conversion of 1 mM adenosine to Ara-AMP in 4 h using 0.05 mM ADP. The modular design was also applicable to guanosine and inosine, affording the corresponding arabinosyl nucleotides, albeit with lower yields. This work establishes a sustainable biocatalytic platform for nucleoside analogues, exemplifying how enzyme promiscuity, thermodynamic driving, and cofactor recycling enable green pharmaceutical manufacturing.

articles.titulo: 7-(Chloroquinolin-4-yl) Sulfanyl Derivatives, Optimization of the Synthesis, In Silico ADMET Profiling Studies, and Evaluation of the Biological Activity Against Leishmania mexicana.
articles.autores: Gelvez A, Labrador-Fagúndez L, Stella BG, Rivero S, Ramirez Y, Vidal T, Martinez-Sotillo N, Suárez A, Chávez K, Ramírez H, Blanco Z, Gutiérrez J, Charris J, Benaim G
articles.resumo_original: Leishmaniasis is a parasitic human infection that constitutes a major global health challenge due to limited therapeutic options, toxicity, resistance, and high costs of the drugs approved as therapy. In this study, a group of 7-chloroquinoline derivatives (5-12) was synthesized via an optimized route and evaluated against the human parasite Leishmania mexicana. Compounds were fully characterized and showed favorable in silico ADME/Tox profiles, including high predicted gastrointestinal absorption (>93%), although limited solubility and potential hepatotoxicity were observed for several derivatives. Biological assays demonstrated significant antileishmanial activity. Interestingly, intracellular amastigote assays revealed nanomolar potency and very high selectivity index (SI), with compound 12 exhibiting IC50 = 2.5 nM (SI = 21.030) and compound 9 IC50 = 5.2 nM (SI = 7.384). Mechanistic studies demonstrated concentration-dependent mitochondrial membrane depolarization and acidocalcisome alkalinization. Since these two organelles are both involved in bioenergetics and in parasite intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis, the results support the notion that intracellular Ca2+ disruption is an essential target for different drug actions. Overall, these findings support a multitarget mechanism and position these quinoline derivatives as promising chemical scaffolds for the development of improved antileishmanial strategies.

articles.titulo: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release.
articles.autores: Jain A, Dong R, Kroll J, Webster JF, Moss J, Bikbaev A, Ultanir SK, Gonzalez-Sulser A, Rosenmund C, Heine M, Liu J, Cousin MA, Ivanova D
articles.resumo_original: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

articles.titulo: Sustainable synthesis of metallic nanoparticles and their potential biotechnological applications.
articles.autores: Ugale SV, Gaikwad SC, Bankar AV, Nawani N
articles.resumo_original: Nanotechnology has emerged as a vital interdisciplinary field with applications in medicine, biotechnology, environmental remediation, agriculture, energy, and advanced materials. Metallic nanoparticles (NPs), typically ranging from 1 to 100 nm, have distinctive physicochemical characteristics, including small size, a high surface-area-to-volume ratio, surface reactivity, and tunable electronic properties. Although conventional physical and chemical methods can effectively control nanoparticle (NP) composition and morphology, they may require high energy inputs, specialized equipment, or potentially toxic reagents. Therefore, biological synthesis strategies using plants, microorganisms, and biologically derived molecules have received much attention as alternative approaches for metallic NP synthesis.This review critically evaluates conventional, biological, and hybrid strategies for synthesizing metallic NPS, with particular emphasis on silver (Ag), copper (Cu), and silver-copper (Ag-Cu) bimetallic nanomaterials. The review also discusses NP's characterization methods, including UV-Visible (UV-Vis) spectroscopy, Electron microscopy (EM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Dynamic light scattering (DLS), zeta-potential analysis, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), while emphasizing the limitations of interpreting any single technique in isolation. This work highlights the transition from laboratory-scale green synthesis to reproducible, scalable nanomanufacturing, including challenges associated with batch-to-batch reproducibility, biological-feedstock variability, purification, process control, safety, toxicity, and life-cycle sustainability. Finally, the review highlights the diverse biotechnological applications of metallic NPs in antimicrobial systems, diagnostics, drug delivery, agriculture, environmental remediation, and related industrial sectors. Overall, the review argues that biological synthesis methods should not automatically be regarded as sustainable. Instead, assess their advantages by integrating material performance, process efficiency, reproducibility, scalability, safety, and environmental impact.

articles.titulo: Biochar-immobilised phosphate-solubilising bacteria enhance soil available phosphorus by affecting phosphorus fraction transformation and phosphorus-acquiring microbiota.
articles.autores: Zhou L, Peng L, Rousk J, Deng H, Mu L, Wang Z, Dai W, Gao M
articles.resumo_original: Phosphate-solubilising bacteria (PSB) play an important role in phosphorus (P) transformation and plant P uptake. However, their effectiveness is often limited by environmental instability and soil poor survival. Biochar has been proposed as a suitable carrier for microbial immobilisation; however, the effects of biochar-immobilised PSB on soil P fractions and the microbial mechanisms underlying P transformation remain unclear. In this study, we developed a biochar-immobilised PSB using Klebsiella sp. N107 and assessed its effects on soil P availability, P fraction transformation, and microbial processes regulating P cycling. A pot experiment was conducted: no fertilisation, conventional fertilisation (NPK), NPK + pristine biochar (NPKB), NPK + PSB (NPKP), and NPK + biochar-immobilised PSB (NPKBP). Soil properties, P fractions, organic acids, enzyme activities, and metagenomic characteristics were analysed. Compared with NPKB and NPKP, NPKBP enhanced plant P uptake and soil available P. It also increased labile P fractions, organic acid concentrations, and the activities of P acquiring enzymes. Genes associated with P transport (pit, ugpB, ugpQ, and ugpE), polyphosphate degradation (ppk1 and ppk2), organic P mineralisation (phoA and phoD), and inorganic P solubilisation (gcd, ppa, and ppx) were upregulated. P acquiring taxa, including Sphingomonas, Gaiella, and Bradyrhizobium, were enriched and contributed functionally to P cycling. Overall, biochar-immobilised PSB improved soil P availability by promoting P fraction transformation and restructuring microbial communities involved in P cycling. Soil pH, organic acids, and available nitrogen were identified as key drivers of these processes, highlighting the potential of biochar-immobilised PSB to improve soil P utilisation and management.

articles.titulo: Pressure Engineering through Silica Nanoconfinement for Melting Point Elevation of Gold Nanoparticles.
articles.autores: Choi CW, Choi JH, Kim GY, Lee IS, Choi SY
articles.resumo_original: Au nanoparticles (NPs) are inherently thermally unstable at elevated temperatures because their large surface-to-volume ratio promotes melting, migration, and coalescence. Here, we demonstrate that silica (SiO2) nanoconfinement thermodynamically elevates the melting point (Tm) of Au NPs through confinement-induced compressive pressure. Atomic-resolution in situ heating scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) combined with local Fourier crystallinity mapping reveals that bare Au NPs lose crystallinity at 1,000 °C, whereas SiO2-encapsulated Au cores (Au@SiO2) remain crystalline. Accordingly, in situ heating TEM shows bare Au NPs progressively merge while Au@SiO2 remain structurally isolated. Temperature-dependent lattice-parameter measurements reveal significantly suppressed thermal expansion of confined Au cores, corresponding to an estimated compressive stress of 4-5 GPa. Finite-element simulations support this estimate, showing that SiO2 shell shrinkage generates several-GPa core pressure, with thicker shells producing higher pressure and greater Tm elevation. These findings establish nanoconfinement-induced pressure as a general thermomechanical strategy for stabilizing metallic NPs under extreme thermal environments.

articles.titulo: Dual-Phosphorylated Pumpkin Seed Protein Pickering Emulsions: Structural Evolution, Interfacial Regulation, and Coffee Creamer Application Quality.
articles.revista: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.autores: Huang J, Wang D, Ruan Z, Xu H, Yang Z, Chen J
articles.resumo_original: Pumpkin seed protein (PSP) was modified with sodium tripolyphosphate (STP) and sodium trimetaphosphate (STMP) to improve Pickering emulsions. Phosphorylation increased with STMP content but plateaued at high ratios. Mass spectrometry identified phosphorylated Ser and Thr residues, while 31P NMR indicated multiple phosphorus environments. Modification altered protein conformation and surface charge, reduced particle size, and improved dispersion without major subunit degradation. Although emulsifying activity decreased, emulsion stability increased; mixed-phosphate treatments generally produced finer droplets and better resistance to centrifugal destabilization than single-phosphate treatments. A 4:1 STP/STMP ratio combined small droplet size with favorable wettability and interfacial adsorption, whereas higher STMP content did not consistently improve overall performance. In coffee beverages, increasing emulsion incorporation intensified phase separation and altered color and flavor. At a 1:9 emulsion-to-coffee ratio, phosphorylated PSP emulsion improved perceived body and smoothness while retaining coffee aroma, outperforming commercial creamer in balance and supporting its potential use as a plant-based food.

articles.titulo: Design, Characterization and In Vivo Evaluation of Rifaximin-Loaded Chitosan Nanoparticles for Potential Colonic Drug Delivery in Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
articles.autores: Deljavan Ghodrati A, Comoglu T
articles.resumo_original: This study aimed to develop rifaximin (RFX) loaded chitosan (CS)-tripolyphosphate (TPP) nanoparticles for potential colonic delivery as a drug delivery system for the management of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Nanoparticles were prepared using the ionotropic gelation method and optimized by varying stirring speed, TPP concentration, and polymer-to-drug ratio. The optimized formulation (F41) exhibited a particle size of 262.4 ± 24.3 nm, a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.389 ± 0.033, a zeta potential of + 9.91 ± 0.94 mV, and an encapsulation efficiency (EE%) of 94.75 ± 0.04%. In vitro release studies demonstrated nearly complete drug release within 36 h, which was faster compared to other formulations (52-64 h). Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirmed spherical morphology, while differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) analyses indicated successful drug encapsulation without chemical interaction. In vivo evaluation using a chronic restraint stress (CRS) induced IBS model showed that F41 significantly improved physiological parameters, including reduced fecal water content (20.655 ± 23.494%), increased body weight gain (22.716 ± 3.903%), and a decreased disease activity index (p < 0.05). These findings indicate that, the optimized nanoparticle system demonstrated favorable physicochemical properties, sustained drug release, and improved therapeutic outcomes. Owing to the cationic nature of CS, the system may also provide enhanced interaction with colonic mucus, potentially contributing to prolonged local residence. These findings suggest that the developed formulation represents promising approach for potential colonic delivery of RFX in IBS management; however, further studies are required to directly evaluate its mucoadhesive properties and underlying mechanisms.

articles.titulo: Revitalizing simultaneous nitrification, endogenous denitrification and phosphorus removal under carbon starvation: Redox mediator-modulated electron transfer and metabolic coordination.
articles.autores: Chen H, Chai Z, Song C, Zheng Y, Chen J, Zheng M
articles.resumo_original: The simultaneous nitrification, endogenous denitrification and phosphorus removal (SNEDPR) process provides a resource-efficient paradigm for synergistic nutrient removal. However, its efficacy can be severely constrained by limited electron-donor availability and inefficient intracellular electron transfer under low carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratios. Herein, we demonstrate that anthraquinone-2-sulfonate (AQS) serves as an effective redox mediator to alleviate these electron-transfer limitations. Under severe carbon-limited conditions, with an influent C/N ratio of 3.24±0.11, supplementation with 0.3 mmol/L AQS successfully restored the deteriorated system, recovering total inorganic nitrogen (TIN) removal efficiency to 96.57±0.87% while sustaining robust phosphorus removal (96.47±2.68%). Batch kinetic assays showed that AQS increased electron transfer system activity (ETSA) by over 100%, accompanied by enhanced nitrification-related activity, endogenous denitrification and phosphorus uptake. Integrated metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analyses further revealed transcriptional responses consistent with an electron-shuttling role of AQS, including enhanced ETC-associated electron-transfer potential and increased transcription of downstream denitrification enzymes. ATP synthase-related transcription was also enhanced, indicating an increased potential for PMF-coupled cellular energy conservation. Consequently, increased transcription was observed for key functional genes involved in nitrification (amoABC, nxrAB), denitrification (narGHI, napAB, nirKS, nosZ), and polyphosphate synthesis (ppk). Furthermore, AQS-amended operation was associated with microbial community succession toward a more specialized consortium, in which comammox, Thauera and Candidatus Accumulibacter clade ⅡC were associated with nitrification, endogenous denitrification, and denitrifying phosphorus removal, respectively. Although practical translation will require effective retention or recovery of soluble AQS, these findings demonstrate the potential of AQS-enhanced SNEDPR under carbon-limited conditions and provide multi-omics evidence linking improved nutrient removal with increased electron-transfer activity and coordinated microbial metabolic responses.

articles.titulo: Effects of Irrigation Protocols on Dentin-Root Interface Integrity and Sealer Penetration after Minimally Invasive versus Conventional Instrumentation: An Ex Vivo Analysis.
articles.autores: Scardini IL, Masiero AV, Dos Santos M, Parolia A, Teixeira FB
articles.resumo_original:
This study compared the effects of ultrasonic activation (UA), laser-activated irrigation (LAI), and the GentleWave® system (GW) on root dentin and sealer penetration (SP) after minimally invasive (MI) and conventional (CT) instrumentation techniques.
One hundred extracted human mandibular premolars were allocated according to the instrumentation technique. Forty teeth (n=20) were analyzed for root dentin morphology using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and 60 teeth (n=30) were assessed for SP using confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM). For SEM analysis, specimens were further subdivided by irrigation protocol, including a negative control group (n=5). For SP evaluation, teeth were subdivided by irrigation protocol (n=10) and obturated with EndoSequence® BC Sealer labeled with 0.003% Fluo-3. Data were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis test and Dunn's post hoc test (p < 0.05).
No significant differences in smear layer (SL) scores were found between CT and MI when the same irrigation technique was compared. In CT-prepared teeth, the control group exhibited higher SL than the irrigation groups, except in the middle third, where the results were comparable to those of UA. In MI-prepared teeth, GW showed lower SL scores than LAI in the cervical third (p < 0.05). In the apical third of MI-prepared canals, GW and LAI were associated with greater sealer penetration area and maximum depth than UA (p < 0.05). Dentin erosion was observed in 15 of 120 (12.5%) imageswith 10 images from the UA group and 5 from the LAI group. No erosion was observed in the GW group.
Under the experimental conditions evaluated, no morphological signs of dentin erosion were observed with the GW protocol, and GW and LAI were associated with greater apical SP than UA following MI instrumentation. Because the protocols differed in irrigant volume, exposure time, and sequence, these findings cannot be attributed specifically to the activation technologies.

articles.titulo: 3D Reconstruction of Nanoparticle Distribution in Tumor Spheroids With Volume Electron Microscopy.
articles.autores: Bottone D, Gerken LRH, Habermann S, Mateos JM, Lucas MS, Riemann J, Fachet M, Resch-Genger U, Kissling VM, Rösslein M, Gogos A, Herrmann IK
articles.resumo_original: Spatially resolved characterization of nanomaterial (NM) distribution within cellular ultrastructure is essential for understanding NM fate and activity in biological systems. Volume electron microscopy (vEM) is uniquely positioned to address this challenge, yet fully documented quantitative pipelines that simultaneously segment NMs and cellular structures remain scarce. Here, an end-to-end analytical pipeline is presented based on the example of serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBF-SEM) data of tumor spheroids containing nanoparticles (NPs). A hybrid segmentation strategy is adopted, comprising a fine-tuned Cellpose-SAM model for cells and nuclei, and an empirical Bayes approach for AuNPs. The fine-tuned model outperforms both the pre-trained baseline and the benchmark experiments in Amira, and shows good generalization to 2D EM datasets of varying sample types, suggesting potential as a general-purpose segmentation model for electron microscopy. Full 3D reconstruction of NP distributions reveals preferential clustering in the perinuclear region, with a median nucleus-to-NP distance of 2.57 μ m  and NM uptake spanning several orders of magnitude across cells. Furthermore, morphological analysis of segmented cells and nuclei using 3D shape descriptors and local curvature metrics provides quantitative access to features inaccessible from single sections. Together, these results establish a reproducible, open framework for the joint quantitative analysis of NM distribution and cellular morphology in vEM data.

articles.titulo: Engineering zero thermal expansion over a wide temperature range in PbTiO3-based ferroelectrics.
articles.autores: Pan Z, Ye M, Suo Y, Wang D, Shen X, Pi M, Zhang G, Ye X, Shen Y, Yu R, Long Y
articles.resumo_original: Thermal expansion mismatches in precision optics, aerospace, and electronics can lead to delamination and fatigue, driving urgent demand for zero thermal expansion (ZTE) materials. At present, the majority of single-phase ZTE materials only function effectively below 500 K, limiting potential applications in many critical fields. Herein, we employ high-pressure and high-temperature synthesis to develop (1 - x)PbTiO3-xBi(Cu3/4W1/4)O3 perovskite ferroelectrics, utilizing spontaneous volume ferroelectrostriction to achieve an ultrawide ZTE regime from 300 to 725 K. In situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction tracks the lattice contraction and phase stability, while transmission electron microscopy provides insights into atomic-scale A/B-site cation displacements and tetragonal distortions. First-principles calculations reveal that polar ferroelectric-active Bi3+, Cu2+, and W6+ ions synergistically reorganize electron density to reinforce ferroelectric distortion, while Cu-derived van Hove singularities near the Fermi level dominate the density of states and govern the elastic anomalies linked to the ultrawide ZTE behaviors. This study extends the scope of high-temperature ZTE materials and establishes a ferroelectric-active ion-doping strategy to engineer thermal expansion.

articles.titulo: Nanoscale Characterization of Microscopically Layered Bone in the Russian Sturgeon Pectoral Fin Spine: A 3D FIB-SEM Study.
articles.revista: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
articles.autores: Marroquín-Arroyave E, Milgram J
articles.resumo_original: Dermal bone, the earliest known form of bone, develops without a cartilage precursor and persists in extant fish species. The pectoral fin spine (PFS) is a dermal bone located at the leading edge of the pectoral fin of sturgeons, where it is exposed to loading associated with locomotion. The peripheral region and dermal osteons of the PFS both appear layered at lower magnification; however, collagen organization in load-bearing fish skeletal elements remains incompletely characterized at the nanoscale. The aim of this study is to characterize the 3D nanostructure of the layered peripheral and osteonal bone forming the PFS in Russian sturgeons using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM). In the dermal osteons, bone forms concentric layers around a central canal at lower magnification, and at the nanoscale, the calcified collagen fibrils within these layers have preferential orientations that change in a clockwise-anticlockwise fanning pattern, consistent with lamellar bone. In contrast, the examined peripheral bone, which also appears layered at low magnification, is composed mainly of unidirectional calcified collagen fibrils aligned with the long axis of the PFS. Within the examined peripheral volumes, no comparable nanoscale lamellar pattern was detected, and the predominant fibril organization was consistent with parallel-fibered bone. Groups of voids associated with unidentified fibrillar material were also observed in the examined peripheral volumes; the voids were oriented approximately normal to the long axis of the PFS. We conclude that regions appearing layered at lower magnification can differ markedly at the nanoscale, and that the lamellar organization seen in dermal osteons raises questions about its evolutionary origin.

articles.titulo: Bromide Sequestration Using a Low-Cost Hybrid Composite of Calcium, Activated Carbon, Kaolin, and Starch.
articles.autores: Al-Mur BA, Jamal MT
articles.resumo_original: Bromide in source waters promotes the formation of toxic brominated disinfection byproducts during chlorination and ozonation, necessitating efficient, affordable pretreatment materials. This study developed a low-cost hybrid composite, denoted Calcium-Activated Carbon-Kaolin-Starch (CAKS) composite, from kaolin, activated carbon, a calcium precursor and starch through starch-assisted consolidation followed by calcination under nitrogen. The synthesized material was characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, nitrogen adsorption-desorption analysis, scanning electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. CAKS exhibited a heterogeneous mesoporous structure with a Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 212.5 m2 g-1, a pore volume of 0.384 cm3 g-1, and an average pore diameter of 7.2 nm. Batch adsorption experiments showed that bromide uptake was strongly dependent on solution pH, adsorbent dosage, contact time, initial concentration, agitation speed, temperature, and the presence of competing ions. Maximum removal of approximately 97.3% was achieved at pH 5, close to the apparent point of zero charge of 5.5. Adsorption was rapid during the first 60 min and approached equilibrium after 90-120 min. The experimental adsorption capacity increased with increasing bromide concentration, reaching approximately 40.0 mg g-1 at an initial bromide concentration of 200 mg L-1. Equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir model, which yielded a model-estimated maximum adsorption capacity of 81.30 mg g-1. Kinetic data were described best by the pseudo-second-order model, although film diffusion and intraparticle diffusion also contributed to the overall uptake process. Equilibrium data indicated heterogeneous adsorption behavior, while thermodynamic analysis suggested that bromide adsorption was thermodynamically favorable under the investigated conditions. Regeneration with 0.1 M Sodium hydroxide and reuse over five adsorption-desorption cycles was also evaluated. Results were obtained under controlled laboratory conditions.

articles.titulo: Interfacial Engineering of Fe3O4/Biochar via CMC Bridging for Durable Lithium/Sodium-Ion Storage.
articles.autores: Li H, Yang Z, Jia C, Li Z, Xia H
articles.resumo_original: The development of cost-effective and durable anode materials derived from renewable biomass is essential for practical lithium- and sodium-ion batteries (LIBs/SIBs). However, conventional strategies for integrating high-capacity metal oxides with biomass carbon often suffer from weak oxide-carbon adhesion, nanoparticle aggregation, and large volume changes during cycling. To overcome these limitations, we present an interfacial engineering approach in which carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) serves as a molecular bridge to anchor Fe3O4 nanoparticles in situ onto ginkgo branch-derived biochar (GBC). The abundant hydroxyl and carboxyl groups of CMC simultaneously guide uniform Fe3O4 nucleation and create a molecular bridge that mediates interfacial chemical interactions that facilitate charge transfer while accommodating volume strain. Structural and compositional analyses confirm the formation of CMC/Fe3O4/GBC with well-dispersed nanocrystals, a hierarchically porous architecture, and magnetic responsiveness. As an anode, CMC/Fe3O4/GBC delivers 256 mAh/g at 2000 mA/g in SIBs, substantially higher than that of bare GBC and unmodified Fe3O4/GBC. Comparable durability is observed in LIBs, where the composite retains 297 mAh/g after 2000 cycles at the same rate. Kinetic studies using cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic intermittent titration technique, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveal that CMC bridging enhances pseudocapacitive contribution and accelerates ion diffusion. Post-cycling X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy further confirm the preserved electrode integrity. These results establish a scalable interfacial modification strategy for biomass-derived magnetic composites toward durable alkali-ion storage.

articles.titulo: Antitumor Activity of a Bupleurum chinense-Derived Vesicle-like Particle Preparation in MOC1 Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Models.
articles.autores: Li S, Zhang G, Zhao L, Wang S, Feng W, Ran X, Ge W
articles.resumo_original: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the antitumor activity of a Bupleurum chinense-derived extracellular vesicle-like particle (BC-EVLP) preparation in MOC1 oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) models. Methods: Fresh roots were processed by differential centrifugation, filtration, ultracentrifugation, and sucrose density-gradient separation. The preparation was characterized by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and total protein measurement. Cellular association, viability, ROS-associated fluorescence, mitochondrial membrane potential, and Annexin V-FITC/PI staining were assessed. Cell viability was also compared after exposure to equal added volumes of the preparation or pre-gradient ultracentrifugation supernatant. Female C57BL/6 mice bearing syngeneic MOC1 tumors received peritumoral treatment every 3 days for 14 days, followed by tumor histology. Results: The preparation contained nanoscale vesicle-like structures, with median and mean particle diameters of 162.0 and 191.9 nm. DiI-associated fluorescence was detected in MOC1 cells after 4 h. Treatment reduced cell viability and was associated with increased DCF fluorescence, a lower JC-1 red/green ratio, and increased Annexin V-positive fractions. The BC-EVLP preparation reduced cell viability more than the supernatant at equal added volumes, although the higher-volume supernatant treatment retained partial activity. High-dose treatment attenuated tumor growth in vivo, and representative tumor sections showed less densely cellular areas. Conclusions: The BC-EVLP preparation exhibited antitumor activity in the tested MOC1 models. The active constituents and the relative contributions of vesicular and non-vesicular components remain unresolved.

articles.titulo: Sustainable Hybrid Flame-Retardant Architectures for LDPE: Effects of Waste-Derived Cellulose, SiO2, and APP/ADA.
articles.autores: Ruiz-Martínez ARY, Cabrera-Álvarez EN, Silva LD, León A, Diaz de León R, Contreras-López D
articles.resumo_original: This study evaluates the flame retardant efficiency of hybrid systems based on natural cellulose extracted from agricultural wastes (pecan nutshell and guayule), combined with azodicarbonamide (ADA), porous silicon dioxide (SiO2) scaffolds, and ammonium polyphosphate (APP), incorporated into low-density polyethylene (LDPE). The waste-derived cellulose fractions were isolated via alkaline extraction and steam explosion, yielding microfibrils that preserved native lignin fractions. Porous SiO2 particles were modified through the adsorption of ADA and APP, which in turn decorated the surface of the cellulose particles. Hybrid LDPE composites containing 20 wt% of total additives were melt-compounded and characterized. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) revealed an early intumescent activation that promoted robust charring, achieving final char residue yields up to 9.5 wt% for the pecan nutshell composite. Horizontal UL-94 and cone calorimeter tests demonstrated the complete elimination of hazardous flaming melt-dripping across all formulated hybrid systems, accompanied by a significant reduction in the burning rate to 18.3 mm/min and a 45% reduction in PHRR for the pecan nutshell-derived compound, consistent with a protective contribution of the multifunctional particles in the condensed phase, significantly outperforming its commercial nanocellulose counterparts. Cone calorimetry highlighted a drastic flattening of the peak heat release rate (PHRR) kinetics of composites. FTIR, TEM and TGA analyses confirmed the formation of a APP-ADA-loaded SiO2 particle scaffold ("grenade-like" morphology), with combustion-residue FTIR and SEM/EDS supporting a protective contribution in the condensed phase.

articles.titulo: Electrostatic multipolar probe-forming objective lens for FIB.
articles.autores: Berdou-Durrieu L, Mellier JB, Fay JB, Salord O, Reveillard M, Warot-Fonrose B, Viteau M, Houdellier F
articles.resumo_original: This paper explores the possibility of using a system of four aligned electrostatic quadrupoles, also known as Russian quadruplet, as an objective lens for a Focused Ion Beam (FIB). The system has been designed compact to be fitted onto standard FIB columns installed in dual beam systems. Each quadrupole has been designed to allow for simple mechanical assembly, whilst retaining the ability to generate an octopole field self-centered with the main quadrupole field by polarizing the ground apertures surrounding the main electrodes. The goal of this additional octopole field will be to compensate for strong aperture aberrations. The performance of this new probe-forming multipole objective lens has been investigated by spot milling a silicon sample's surface using both LMIS and plasma sources. Probe-forming properties and beam shape affected by aperture aberrations of the new Russian quadruplet objective lens are then observed by Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) images and compared with standard spots observed using conventional rotational symmetric einzel lens. Using an LMIS source, we were able to focus spots with sizes, depending on the current range, at least equivalent to those obtained with conventional optics, while maintaining a working distance more than three times greater. In particular, at low currents in the tens-of-picoampere range, spot diameters of 200 nanometers were achieved, which are half the size of conventional spots. At high currents in the hundred-of-nanoamperes range, spot diameters in the micrometer range were achieved. The results obtained with a plasma source made it possible to generate spots in the tens-of-micrometers range at high currents, while maintaining the advantage of the large working distance. However, for long etching times in the hundred of seconds, a long "evanescent line" is observed along one direction. We will discuss its origin and propose ways to correct this artifact. Finally a first milling application using focused ion lines is also presented at the end of this work.

articles.titulo: Upcycling Used Tyre Rubber into Carbon Adsorbents: Effect of Physical Activation on Porous Structure and Comparative Evaluation for p-Chlorophenol Removal.
articles.autores: Troca-Torrado C, Alexandre-Franco MF, Garrido-Zoido JM, Cuerda-Correa EM, Gómez-Serrano V
articles.resumo_original: The porous architecture of carbons derived from polymeric waste is largely governed by the physical activation atmosphere. In this work, used tyre rubber (UTR) was converted into carbonaceous adsorbents by pyrolysis followed by physical activation in air, CO2 or steam. The influence of the activation route on porous structure, surface chemistry and adsorption performance was systematically investigated. The materials were characterised by N2 adsorption at -196 °C, mercury intrusion porosimetry, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), FT-IR spectroscopy and point-of-zero-charge (pHpzc) measurements. The resulting materials were evaluated for the removal of p-chlorophenol from aqueous solution and comparatively assessed against three commercial carbon materials. Steam activation proved to be the most effective treatment, increasing the BET surface area from 64 to 344 m2 g-1 and the micropore volume from 0.05 to 0.23 cm3 g-1 while generating a hierarchical micro-/mesoporous structure that significantly enhanced pore accessibility and mass transport. Among the UTR-derived carbons, the steam-activated sample exhibited the highest equilibrium p-Cp uptake and adsorption kinetics approaching those of a commercial activated carbon despite its lower specific surface area. Kinetic and equilibrium analyses demonstrated that adsorption performance depends not only on the extent of microporosity but also on pore accessibility and network connectivity, highlighting the critical role of transport mesoporosity in facilitating molecular diffusion towards adsorption sites. The adsorption results are consistent with an important contribution from accessible microporosity, while π-π interactions between p-chlorophenol and aromatic carbon domains may also contribute. These findings demonstrate that tailoring porous structure through physical activation provides an effective strategy for transforming UTR into high-performance carbon adsorbents and establishes robust processing-structure-property relationships that can guide the rational design of waste-derived carbon adsorbents.

articles.titulo: Effect of Build Orientation on the Electrical, Thermal, and Mechanical Properties of PA12 Fabricated by Selective Laser Sintering.
articles.autores: Huang L, Tu S, Lyu Y, Tu Y, Li H
articles.resumo_original: Selective laser sintering (SLS) provides a promising route for the rapid fabrication of polymeric insulating components with complex geometries. However, its layer-by-layer manufacturing process inherently introduces structural anisotropy, which may significantly affect the electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties of the printed materials. In this study, polyamide 12 (PA12) specimens fabricated by SLS at different printing orientations were systematically investigated for dielectric properties, volume resistivity, DC and AC breakdown strength, tensile properties, and thermal conductivity. Scanning electron microscopy and X-ray microscopy were further employed to characterize the microstructure and clarify the origin of the anisotropic behavior. The results show that SLS-printed PA12 exhibits pronounced orientation-dependent properties. As the printing angle increases from 0° to 90°, the volume resistivity and DC breakdown strength generally decrease. In contrast, the relative permittivity generally increases with printing angle, whereas the AC breakdown strength and dielectric loss exhibit more complex non-monotonic variations. The tensile strength and elongation at break both gradually decrease with increasing printing angle. The thermal conductivity varies only slightly across different orientations but increases overall with printing angle. Microstructural observations reveal numerous interlayer pores, incompletely sintered regions, and heterogeneous interfaces with a distinct layered distribution. These heterogeneous interlayer structures affect the transport of charge, heat, and load, thereby contributing to the anisotropic electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties of SLS-printed PA12. These findings provide a basis for optimizing the printing orientation and structural design of SLS-printed PA12 for high-voltage insulation applications.

articles.titulo: Polyphosphate-Functionalized PGMA-Grafted Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles for Selective U(VI) Removal from Aqueous Solutions.
articles.autores: Alshammari AS, Alosime EM, Basfar AA
articles.resumo_original: Uranium(VI) contamination in aquatic environments poses significant environmental and public health concerns, creating a need for efficient and selective adsorbents. In this study, polyphosphate-functionalized poly(glycidyl methacrylate)-grafted mesoporous silica nanoparticles (PP-PGMA/MSNs) were successfully synthesized and evaluated for U(VI) removal from aqueous solutions. A key novelty of this work lies in the incorporation of phosphate-rich functionalities onto PGMA-grafted MSNs prepared via ATRP, together with the systematic investigation of their effects on U(VI) adsorption equilibrium and selectivity in multi-metal systems. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) confirmed the successful incorporation of phosphate-containing functional groups onto the MSN surface. The adsorbent exhibited rapid adsorption, reaching equilibrium within 120 min, with optimum performance observed at pH 4-6. A maximum U(VI) removal efficiency of 73.81% was achieved at an initial concentration of 10 mg L-1, while the maximum adsorption capacity reached 114.94 mg g-1. Equilibrium data were well described by the Langmuir isotherm model (R2 = 0.9697), indicating predominantly monolayer adsorption on relatively homogeneous adsorption sites. Despite a substantial reduction in surface area following functionalization, the material maintained a high adsorption capacity, suggesting that uranium uptake is governed primarily by interactions at phosphate-containing active sites. Furthermore, the adsorbent exhibited preferential affinity toward U(VI) in multi-metal systems containing Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, and Pb ions, demonstrating enhanced selectivity toward uranyl species. The adsorption behavior suggests that phosphate functionalities serve as the primary binding sites through surface complexation and coordination interactions. These findings demonstrate the potential of PP-PGMA/MSNs as selective adsorbents for U(VI) removal from complex aqueous systems and environmental remediation applications.

articles.titulo: Electrospun Carbon Nanofiber-TiN Composite Interlayers for Improved Cycling Stability and Rate Capability of Lithium-Sulfur Batteries.
articles.autores: Niu C, Liu H, Chao Z
articles.resumo_original: Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries offer a high theoretical energy density of 2600 Wh·kg-1 and a theoretical specific capacity of 1675 mAh·g-1; however, their practical application is severely hindered by the shuttle effect of soluble lithium polysulfides, the intrinsic electronic insulating nature of sulfur and Li2S, and the substantial volume variation during charge/discharge processes. In this study, titanium nitride (TiN) powder was first prepared, and a carbon nanofiber/titanium nitride (CNF@TiN) composite nanofiber membrane was subsequently fabricated by electrospinning followed by pre-oxidation/carbonization treatment and employed as a functional interlayer between the separator and sulfur cathode. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) showed that the obtained TiN possessed a well-crystallized face-centered cubic structure. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) revealed that TiN particles were relatively uniformly dispersed and anchored within the three-dimensional interconnected CNF network. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analyses of the composite and the TiN powder confirmed the presence of Ti-N bonding, revealed N/O-containing functional groups on the carbon scaffold, and indicated only a thin oxidized layer on the TiN particle surface. Nitrogen adsorption-desorption analysis confirmed the porous character of the fibrous interlayers. Electrochemical tests showed that the cell equipped with the CNF@TiN interlayer delivered an initial discharge specific capacity of 1205 mAh·g-1 at 0.1 C and retained a reversible capacity of approximately 1010 mAh·g-1 after 100 cycles. At 0.2 C, the initial discharge specific capacity was approximately 1065 mAh·g-1, and approximately 875 mAh·g-1 was retained after 300 cycles, corresponding to a capacity retention of 82.2% and an average capacity decay of approximately 0.059% per cycle. Rate capability, cyclic voltammetry (CV), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and galvanostatic charge-discharge measurements indicated that the CNF@TiN interlayer favors reversible sulfur-species conversion and improved interfacial reaction kinetics. The enhanced performance can be attributed to the physical confinement, electron-transport, and structural-support functions of the CNF network, together with the polar TiN interface, whose presence is consistent with restricted polysulfide migration and facilitated interfacial conversion. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing multifunctional interlayers integrating electrical conductivity, physical confinement, and interfacial regulation for Li-S batteries.

articles.titulo: Chemical and Biological Mobilization of Soil Phosphorus by ppk-Expressing Transgenic Rice (Oryza sativa L.).
articles.autores: Yang S, Wang M, Song X, Wang C, Zhang Y, He D, Yin J, Ge X, Pan L, Xu M, Wei Y, Yang L
articles.resumo_original: Phosphorus (P) availability in alkaline soils is constrained by the immobilization of legacy P, particularly through calcium phosphate precipitation. We used a confined soil-plant microcosm to examine how expression of the polyphosphate kinase gene (ppk) is associated with legacy P utilization in rice (Oryza sativa L.). We compared ppk-expressing transgenic rice (ETR) carrying single-copy (ETRS) and double-copy (ETRD) insertions with their isogenic wild type (WT), without P fertilization. Both transgenic lines had higher root organic acid release and acid phosphatase activity on day 30 and greater plant P acquisition by day 60 than WT; soil pH declined to a greater extent. On day 30, transgenic roots released more oxalate and malate, and their exudates mobilized more soil P than WT exudates in a separate incubation assay. These traits corresponded to greater depletion of the operationally defined HCl-P and NaOH-P pools. Bacterial profiles and PICRUSt2 predictions were descriptive because one pooled library per genotype precluded tests of genotype effects. Diffusive gradients in thin films (DGT) measurements revealed greater rhizosphere labile P in the ETRD early in plant growth, followed by a decline as plant P concentrations increased. This pattern was consistent with an early increase in P supply followed by plant-driven depletion. Net P acquisition in ETRD was 2.55 times that in WT, and ETRD exhibited 53% greater root biomass, while ETRS showed intermediate responses. Collectively, these results link enhanced plant P acquisition to greater P release in exudate incubation assays and higher acid phosphatase activity within this confined system.

articles.titulo: The Impact of Intra-Burst Energy Distribution on Volume Removal and Surface Quality in Laser Ablation of Stainless Steels Using Ultrashort Pulsed Lasers.
articles.autores: Obergfell D, Soldera F, Azarhoushang B, Lasagni AF
articles.resumo_original: Stainless-steel alloys are widely used in applications requiring high corrosion resistance and mechanical durability. For embossing tool fabrication, high-volume material removal with high surface quality is essential. Laser-based ablation offers an alternative to micromilling by enabling material removal without mechanical contact, thereby eliminating cutting tool wear and facilitating the fabrication of complex geometries. However, productivity must be increased without degrading surface quality, which plays a critical role in embossing tool wear behavior and lifetime. This study investigates the ablation efficiency and surface quality of AISI 304, AISI 420, and AISI 316Ti stainless steels using a 250 fs pulsed laser. Different fluence levels and burst configurations, including MHz, GHz, and Bi-burst, are examined, focusing on the influence of intra-burst energy distribution on material removal rate and surface quality. Surface morphology and roughness are characterized by optical, confocal, and scanning electron microscopy. The results show that removal rate, ablation efficiency, and surface roughness are strongly affected by the intra-burst energy distribution (positive or negative slopes). The highest removal rate of 5.74 mm3 min-1 was obtained using MHz bursts, whereas GHz bursts enabled surface roughness values Sa below 1 µm. Negative energy slopes generally reduced surface roughness in isolated MHz and GHz burst modes, while Bi-burst processing provided smooth surfaces over a wider range of slope conditions. All alloys followed similar trends, with AISI 316Ti exhibiting greater susceptibility to microhole formation under certain burst conditions.

articles.titulo: In situ multimodal imaging reveals compartmentalization of reovirus replication factories.
articles.autores: Ďurinová E, Bily T, Kitzberger F, Franta Z, Mojzeš P, Chlanda P, Tuma R
articles.resumo_original: Avian reovirus (ARV) belongs to Reoviridae family of viruses with segmented dsRNA genomes. ARV is responsible for significant economic losses to the poultry industry by causing tenosynovitis and chronic respiratory disease in chickens. ARV virion exhibits an outer protein shell enclosing an inner core, which contains 10 unique dsRNA segments and multiple copies of viral polymerase. ARV assembly takes place in so-called viral factories (VFs). They are cytoplasmic membrane-less inclusions, which accumulate viral proteins and RNA and assist capsid assembly, genome packaging and replication. VFs also provide protection from the host cell defence mechanisms by sequestering viral RNA. Given the dense nature of VFs, little is known about ARV assembly and packaging intermediates. To determine the architecture of VFs across the different length scales and infection course, we employed a wide range of imaging methods. Our data reveal that spherical and fluid VF enriched in viral protein σNS become surrounded by σNS-depleted solid-like compartments at late stages of infection. We demonstrate that confocal Raman microscopy allows label-free imaging of VF composition. Volume electron microscopy, along with electron tomography (ET) and in situ cryo-ET, revealed that the inner phase of VF concentrates viral non-structural proteins and assists assembly of viral cores. The larger, RNA-filled and double-layered particles are assembled at the periphery of the inner fluid phase of VF, forming ordered virion arrays. This suggests that ARV VFs are functionally compartmentalized: the inner fluid phase assists RNA assortment and core particle assembly, whereas the peripheral phase is the site of RNA replication inside viral cores and virion completion.

articles.titulo: Fragment-Linked Purine Derivatives as Inhibitors of (p)ppGpp Synthetases: Design, Synthesis, and Structure-Activity Relationships.
articles.autores: Abdalrahman RAM, Erlitz KS, Massa J, Mais CN, Bange G, Junker A, Koch O
articles.resumo_original: The bacterial stringent response, mediated by the alarmone nucleotides (p)ppGpp, plays a central role in persistence of infections, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial tolerance, making (p)ppGpp synthetases attractive targets for novel antibacterial strategies/therapies. In this study, we report the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of fragment-linked nucleobase derivatives targeting the RelA/SpoT homolog (RSH) enzymes. Guided by structural insights into adenine and guanine binding within small alarmone synthetase (SAS2/RelP), a series of purine-based compounds was developed to simultaneously occupy conserved nucleotide-binding regions. Initial linker-bridged analogues showed limited activity, primarily due to poor solubility, prompting the introduction of ribose-containing derivatives to improve physicochemical properties. Biochemical evaluation using HPLC-based assays revealed selective inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus SAS1, with the most potent compound displaying micromolar activity (IC50 = 1.8 µM), while little or no inhibition was observed for related SAS enzymes. Structure-activity relationship analysis highlights the importance of linker length and nucleobase positioning for enzyme selectivity. These findings establish fragment-linked nucleobase scaffolds as a promising starting point for the development of inhibitors targeting (p)ppGpp biosynthesis and the bacterial stringent response.

articles.titulo: Self-adaptive layered oxide cathodes driven by charge reconfiguration for sodium-ion batteries.
articles.autores: Li JY, Guo Y, Wang X, Pang WK, Hu HY, Zhu YF, Chen D, Liu XY, Gu QF, Johannessen B, Zheng X, Sun Y, Cheng S, Yuan Y, Wu C, Wang JZ, Dou SX, Xiao Y
articles.resumo_original: Layered oxide cathodes have attracted worldwide attention due to environmentally friendliness, structural diversity, and economic benefits. However, poor long-term cycling and unsatisfactory rate performance hinder the practical application. Hence, an oxide cathode with self-adaptive volume has been designed, achieving stable capacity retention of 82% after 1000 cycles at 2 C. The enhanced long-term performance is attributed to its dynamically adjustable volume reducing the acceleration of stress, enabled by a tunable interlayer distance that expands at the beginning of the charging process and then compresses at the highest voltage. Uniform electric field distribution is depicted by 4-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy showing even Coulombic interactions between the oxide layers leading to high mechanical integrity. Such self-adaptable behavior originates from the reduced repulsive force between interlayered oxygen due to the charge reconfiguration of intralayer oxygen and transition metal ions. Additionally, the charge compensation behavior is detected by in situ X-ray absorption spectra, which would be beneficial to high-rate performance. The self-adaptive volume change driven by charge reconfiguration provides a pathway toward durable materials for sustainable sodium-ion energy storage.

articles.titulo: Particle Morphometrics of Glycopyrronium-Formoterol-Budesonide Inhalation Blends Influence Pulmonary Deposition and Bronchodilator Response in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): A Gamma Scintigraphy Study.
articles.autores: Jain GK, Mishra A, Chandra N, Madan M
articles.resumo_original:
The therapeutic efficacy of inhaled triple-combination therapy in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) depends on efficient delivery to peripheral airways. This study evaluated the influence of particle morphometrics on pulmonary deposition and bronchodilator response to glycopyrronium-formoterol-budesonide (GFB) inhalation formulations.
Three commercial GFB formulations (X, Y, and Z) delivered via metered-dose inhaler (MDI) and dry powder inhaler (DPI) were characterized using dynamic light scattering and scanning electron microscopy. In a randomized, open-label pilot study, twenty-four patients with mild-to-moderate COPD inhaled technetium-99m (99mTc) radiolabeled formulations. Regional lung deposition was assessed by planar gamma scintigraphy, and central-to-peripheral (C/P) ratios were calculated. Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) was measured at baseline and 30 minutes post-inhalation.
Significant inter-brand differences in particle morphometrics were observed. Brand X demonstrated a narrow particle distribution (1.3±0.26 µm) with uniform spherical morphology, while brands Y and Z showed relatively broader, polydisperse distributions with irregular particles. MDIs (MIX, MIY, MIZ) consistently outperformed DPIs (DIX, DIY, DIZ), producing greater total lung deposition (23.4% vs 13.7%; P < 0.001) and improved peripheral deposition. Among MDIs, MIX achieved higher intrathoracic deposition (28.8 ± 2.2% vs 19.0-22.5%; P < 0.001) and peripheral deposition (15.8 ± 3.0% vs 9.8-11.5%; P = 0.012), with a lower C/P ratio (0.82 vs 0.96-1.0). Greater spirometric improvement correlated with enhanced deposition, with the MIX producing the highest FEV1 increase (12.8%; P < 0.05).
The findings suggest that particle size distribution, polydispersity, and surface morphology may influence pulmonary deposition and acute spirometric response in COPD. A relatively narrow respirable particle distribution may support more consistent peripheral airway deposition and short-term spirometric response.

articles.titulo: Ablation of Tnfr1 Gene Impairs Enamel Surface Microhardness and Mineral Composition in Mice.
articles.revista: The International journal of developmental biology
articles.autores: Gonçalves JL, Almeida-Júnior LA, Arnez MFM, Galo R, Queiroz AM, Carvalho FK, Paula-Silva FWG
articles.resumo_original: While the immune response is increasingly suspected to play a role in dental enamel defects, the specific pathways involved remain unclear. This study investigated the effects of Tnfrsf1a (TNF receptor superfamily member 1A) gene ablation on amelogenesis and enamel biomineralization. Male Tnfrsf1a knockout (Tnfrsf1a-/-) and wild-type (C57BL/6) mice (n = 6 per group) were evaluated. Lower incisors were analyzed using visual photography, micro-computed tomography (microCT), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), surface microhardness testing, and energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy. Protein expression of MMP20, RUNX2, and AMBN was assessed via immunohistochemistry, while in situ zymography quantified MMP gelatinolytic activity. Gene expression was analyzed using RT-qPCR. Tnfrsf1a-/- mice exhibited no macroscopic opacities, though incisors displayed a distinct whitish coloration. While microCT and SEM revealed no significant differences in enamel volume, or prism ultrastructure, the enamel of Tnfrsf1a-/- mice showed significantly lower calcium and phosphorus content and reduced surface microhardness. Molecular analysis revealed that the Ambn gene was significantly upregulated during both the secretion and maturation stages in Tnfrsf1a-/- mice compared to wild-type controls. Ablation of Tnfrsf1a results in enamel color change in mice characterized by altered mineral composition, reduced mechanical hardness, and dysregulated Ambn expression. These findings suggest that TNF signaling acts as a critical modulator during amelogenesis and is essential for achieving the final mineral quality of dental enamel.

articles.titulo: A conserved insect transcobalamin-like gene is associated with vitamin B12-related functions in the silkworm Bombyx mori.
articles.autores: Xiang JH, Wu Y, Xie QH, Chen BZ, Yi MY, Li FY, Tong XL, Feng QL, Wang M, Xiang H
articles.resumo_original: Vitamin B12 (VB12, cobalamin) is delivered by transcobalamin-dependent pathways in mammals, but comparable host-encoded factors and functions in insects remain unclear. Here we identify a single transcobalamin-like gene in the silkworm Bombyx mori ( Bmtcn) and detect homologs across diverse insect orders. Structure prediction and docking suggest that insect transcobalamin (TCN)-like proteins retain a conserved fold and a pocket compatible with cobalamin binding, although direct biochemical validation remains needed. Bmtcn expression is enriched in the head and is detectable across neuronal and glial populations, implicating the nervous system as a potential site of cobalamin handling and/or demand. Bmtcn loss-of-function mutants accumulate homocysteine, display behavioral abnormalities, and show brain-associated phenotypes. Head transcriptomics reveals coordinated changes consistent with perturbed folate-one-carbon metabolism and broad remodeling of core cellular programs alongside stress-associated responses in the mutants. Because insects lack canonical cobalamin-dependent methionine synthase, these findings suggest that cobalamin may act through alternative metabolic and/or signaling routes. Together, our results implicate a conserved insect transcobalamin-like component in vitamin B12-linked physiology and B. mori as a tractable system for mechanistic dissection.

articles.titulo: Regulation of miR-219 and its target RalGPS is essential for synaptic plasticity at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction.
articles.revista: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.autores: Aavula K, Heggeness H, Yokokura T, Artavanis-Tsakonas S, Van Vactor D
articles.resumo_original: RNA regulatory mechanisms mediate adaptive responses relying on rapid changes in gene expression. By examining microRNA (miRNA)-mediated control of structural synaptic plasticity, we find miR-219 and five other conserved miRNAs regulate activity-induced morphogenesis at Drosophila glutamatergic synapses. Among miRNA targets downregulated by acute stimulation, the Ral activating factor RalGPS is necessary for presynaptic morphogenesis and is sufficient to block plasticity. We find that RalGPS must be held within a narrow range of expression for structural remodeling to occur. Loss or excess of RalGPS both abolish activity-induced synapse growth. Without altering levels of mature miR-219, stimulation elevates miR-219 loading in Argonaute (Ago1)-containing complexes that mediate miRNA gene silencing. We also find that elevated Protein Kinase A activity suppresses miR-219 association with Ago1 and blocks activity-induced synaptic growth, suggesting that miRNA loading and unloading in neurons are both controlled by activity-dependent regulation of Ago1.

articles.titulo: Calcium permeability-enhancing mutations in GluRIIC suppress sustained presynaptic homeostatic plasticity triggered by loss of GluRIIA.
articles.revista: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.autores: Malak OA, Gray L, Aly A, Ball RW, Gustin-Murray J, Moujahidine M, Carrasco G, Rosko A, Isacoff EY, Haghighi AP
articles.resumo_original: Presynaptic homeostatic plasticity (PHP) stabilizes neural circuits by adjusting synaptic strength when faced with disturbances in postsynaptic activity. Despite identification of many genes and mechanisms required for PHP, the underlying trigger mechanisms remain elusive. Loss of GluRIIA, one of five glutamate receptor subunits at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction (NMJ), reduces quantal size and synaptic calcium influx and triggers a sustained PHP. Two common features of genetic manipulations that lead to the activation of this form of PHP are a drop in synaptic calcium influx and a reduction in quantal size; however, it is not clear that either of these features is absolutely necessary for PHP. We have generated a glutamate receptor transgene with mutations in the pore, which can largely restore calcium influx in GluRIIA-/- mutant larvae without affecting quantal size. We find that restoration of calcium influx in GluRIIA-/- mutant larvae blocks PHP without any detectable changes in synaptic structure. Our findings, therefore, indicate that a reduction in synaptic calcium influx is necessary for triggering and/or maintenance of the sustained PHP at the NMJ, a model that may be extendable to the vertebrate NMJ and neuron-neuron synapses.

articles.titulo: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking.
articles.autores: Pugliese SM, Chou GM, Abe ETT, Turcu D, Lancaster JK, Tuthill JC, Brunton BW
articles.resumo_original: Animal locomotion relies on rhythmic body movements driven by central pattern generators (CPGs): neural circuits that produce oscillating output without oscillating input. However, the circuit structure of a CPG for walking is not known in any animal1,2. To identify the cells and synapses that underlie rhythmic leg movement in walking flies, we developed dynamic simulations of the Drosophila ventral nerve cord connectomes3-6. A computational activation screen of descending neurons from the central brain identified DNg100-a known command neuron for walking-as the strongest driver of rhythmic leg motor activity. Simulated network pruning isolated a minimal rhythm-generating circuit consisting of one inhibitory and two excitatory interneurons; this three-neuron circuit was necessary and sufficient for motor rhythms across all six legs and in four connectome datasets. Simulations also predicted that a separate descending pathway (DNb08) drives rhythmic leg movements, which we confirmed experimentally using optogenetics in behaving flies. Our results reveal the cellular identity and synaptic structure of a putative CPG circuit for walking and other rhythmic leg movements in flies.

articles.titulo: Using High-Performance Liquid Chromatography to Study Alterations in Biogenic Amines in Drosophila Models of Brain Disorders.
